text:
Alex: Customer reported 502/SSL errors hitting private inference endpoint after moving to their VPC. Works from our hosted network but fails from their app tier. Error: "TLS handshake failure / connection reset". Seen after ~30s of steady traffic then flips to errors.
Liza: Oof. Do we have their repro steps / app logs? Could be NACL or ephemeral port return traffic blocked.
Alex: They attached client logs: "curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer" and server side just shows incomplete TLS handshake. They also say only high concurrency triggers it.
Priya: High concurrency -> many simultaneous outbound connections from their front tier to inference. If NACL is stateful? NACLs are stateless, need explicit ephemeral port ranges for return. Ask them for their subnet NACL rules and SGs.
Alex: They provided NACL JSON. Inbound rules allow 443, outbound rules only allow a few specific ports (80, 443, 1025-1028). Looks suspicious.
Sam: Yep, that would break returning TCP ephemeral ports. For Linux clients, remote ephemeral ports are >32768 by default. NACL must allow ephemeral ranges back. Suggest repro: run tcpdump on their client side while hitting endpoint.
Alex: Sent repro command to customer: 
```
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and (port 443 or portrange 32768-61000)' -w /tmp/capture.pcap
curl -v https://private-infer.foo.internal/model -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
```
They returned pcap with lots of SYN retransmits and RST from their gateway IP.
Priya: That lines up. Also check their NAT gateway / firewall appliance—some appliances do ephemeral port pinning or conntrack limits and will RST when hit. Ask: are they using a stateful firewall in front of the subnet?
Alex: They said they have a third-party virtual FW in the route table for egress.
Liza: Two likely causes: 1) NACL outbound too restrictive (stateless) so return packets get dropped, 2) middlebox (FW/NAT) has conntrack exhaustion or strict port translation.
Sam: Quick check for TLS certificate issues: run openssl s_client to confirm SNI/cert match from their app hosts: 
```
openssl s_client -connect private-infer.foo.internal:443 -servername private-infer.foo.internal
```
If that fails with "no peer certificate" or "handshake: unsupported protocol" then it's a cert/TLS mismatch. But their server logs showed incomplete handshake rather than cert verify errors.
Alex: We asked them to run both tcpdump and openssl. They ran openssl successfully from one host (low concurrency) but fails when run in parallel 200x (they scripted it).
Priya: That strongly suggests NAT/conntrack limit. Check their firewall logs for TCP RST rate and conntrack counters: `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`.
Alex: Customer posted conntrack_count at ~120k and max 128k, so they are near the limit. They also have a middlebox applying RST when table full.
Liza: Actionable: increase nf_conntrack_max, tune timeout for ESTABLISHED, or put a dedicated NAT with higher capacity. Also open ephemeral return ports on NACLs (e.g., 1024-65535 or the smaller ephemeral range they use).
Sam: For immediate workaround, have them lower client ephemeral port reuse so fewer concurrent sockets per source IP (not ideal). Also consider enabling connection pooling to inference to reduce new TCP/TLS setups.
Alex: I drafted recommended steps for them: 1) Add outbound NACL rule allowing ephemeral range 32768-61000 (or specific range they use). 2) If using a stateless NACL, add symmetric inbound allow for those ephemeral ports. 3) Check/scale their NAT or firewall conntrack limits, increase nf_conntrack_max, and monitor. 4) Validate SNI and TLS with `openssl s_client` once conntrack issue mitigated. 5) Consider putting their app behind multiple source IPs (autoscaling NAT) or our dedicated private peering for high concurrency.
Priya: Also told them to check kernel conntrack timeouts: `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`—lowering can free entries faster but affects long-lived flows.
infra-bot: deploy-check: Recommended docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/private/vpc#egress and https://docs.redwood.ai/troubleshooting/conntrack-nat (link previews disabled).
Alex: Customer accepted plan, will apply ephemeral NACL rule and bump conntrack. Follow-up scheduled in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
Liza: Nice. Add a note to the ticket recommending app-level connection reuse to avoid future issues.
Alex: Will update the support case and close thread after confirm. Thanks all. :pray:
